provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: conclusion length only: the Tours Mame 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam) stops at the short cue; the words that follow it in the witness ('contra persecutores Ecclesix, vel pro Papa') are the book's own rubric, not part of the prayer, and the 1962 continues 'regnat.'; pointing was NOT collated: this comparison is word-level, because the witness reaches me as an optical text layer whose commas, colons and full stops are unreliable. Corroboration: Pustet Ratisbon 1862: Pustet Ratisbon 1862, printed p. 30 (nearest preceding printed-folio marker at text-layer line 65409); text-layer lines 65490-65496 (word-coverage of the 1962 body 0.862); Venice 1570 corroborates at Venice 1570, text-layer lines 63385-63400 (body coverage 0.586, degraded OCR, long s read as f; corroboration only). Recorded limitation: Antecedent taken from the Tours Mame 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam). Word-coverage of the 1962 body at this locus 1.0, of the whole oration 0.941. Every 1862 and Mame reading in this lane rests on an optical text layer, not on a page image; 3 word(s) in this passage were damaged by the recogniser and were read against the 1962 wording rather than off the page - L56410 'RESTA,' read as 'presta'; L56410 'quéesumus,' read as 'quesumus'; L56416 'preedixit' read as 'predixit'. What was NOT checked: the pointing, the ornamental initials, and the printed page of the 1862 beyond the nearest folio marker.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Praesta, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus: ut familia tua per viam salutis
incedat; et, beati Joannis Praecursoris hortamenta sectando, ad eum, quem
praedixit, secura perveniat, Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum:
Qui tecum vivit et regnat.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
